title: Astra rigged and animated digitigrade mech leg walking in 30 minutes
author: nickick_
selftext:
This was wayyy better than every other model I've tried for this before, no other model seemed to understand how to make digitigrade work.

Workflow was Midjourney -> Meshy 7 for GLB with textures -> ask Astra to animate walking in Godot

"can you rig and animate /Users/.../Meshy\_AI\_Iron\_Sentinel\_0907002041\_texture.glb I want to see the digitigrade legs walking convincingly in a Godot preview please"

replies.author: feralferrous
replies.body: Yeah, it's impressive that it pulled that off with just a prompt, until you actually look at the walk cycle and realize it's terrible.  Maybe it's because the model itself is weird?  I suspect it would look funny if it had it's feet /  hips actually pointed in the right directions to begin with.

replies.author: nickick_
replies.body:
I guess I agree compared to production rigging and animation? Still impressive for the workflow that I used: one Midjourney prompt, a few clicks on Meshy, and then a single ask to animate through Astra. 

I'll try prompting something higher fidelity to see how that goes.

comments.author: tabaxi_gf
comments.body: Why is astra rigging and animating the latest meme thing 10 people are posting an hour?  Good to know it can do this but I’m sure it’s not the only thing it’s good at.

replies.author: nickick_
replies.body:
Makes sense to me - it's a visually impressive example of an extreme capability jump by Astra over literally every other AI in existence.   
  
Also I'm sharing one of those "holy shiiiii" moments when I tried doing what everyone's been posting about and it ACTUALLY WORKED in minutes instead of 6 hours and a full week's worth of tokens later.
